Observed at the trial head (decision record, 'Root causes'): two further incompatibilities. unittest.IsolatedAsyncioTestCase instances hold a contextvars.Context, which cannot be pickled, so a suite that holds one is never sent to a worker even when every test in it would be skipped; and four classes built by type() in tests/test_adoption_version_probes.py are not importable under their __qualname__.

predeclared_metrics.quality_rule: Fixed before any hosted run. CORPUS: the whole suite at the draft pull request's head SHA on actual GitHub-hosted macos-15 and ubuntu-24.04 runners. Every job asserts that SHA, because a pull_request checkout is otherwise the merge commit. The trial lock is installed in every arm. Each arm runs three times (fail-fast false; max-parallel 2 on macOS and 4 on Linux; repeat-major order, rotated by one arm per repeat). ORACLE PART 1 is compare.py with its README rules, as frozen here, run with --expected-sha set to the head. An arm-run is ineligible on any of these: (a) a missing or invalid log.txt, exit-code.txt or meta.json; (b) meta.json disagreeing with its directory name; (c) a command other than the arm's preregistered command token for token (README.md 'Arms'; only S may append --durations N), so a token before -m such as an interpreter flag or a wrapper, a reordering, another spelling or an extra argument is ineligible; (d) a checkout_sha other than the head, or a python_version other than S's on that OS; (e) a truncated log or a failed self-consistency check (started tests equal Ran N, records per outcome equal the status line, the status word agrees with the counts, the error report lists exactly the failing records); (f) an exit status that disagrees with the status line, compared as zero versus non-zero only; (g) a unittest-parallel header that is missing (parallel) or present (serial), or a worker count other than min(suites, jobs); (h) executed ids that are not exactly the trial inventory (ids.py on the head; tests behind a failed or skipped setUpClass or setUpModule count as accounted), so every id of the seven gate-step modules must run; (i) any (test id, outcome) record that differs from the first eligible S run of that OS; (j) a runtime.json that is missing or records no run_attempt, or a run_attempt above 1. Ids whose records differ among the eligible S repeats are flaky ids: they are excluded from (i), listed in result.json and named in the observed record. No id is exempt in advance: the three tests that failed on macOS only from 2026-09-25 to 2026-10-02 (limitations) are judged like every other id. ORACLE PART 2: every run directory's git-status.txt (the checkout's git status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=all after the run) exists and is empty; a missing file, the recorder's text 'git status failed' or any content makes the run ineligible. compare.py applies part 2 to every run directory, the control and crash runs included, and the workflow's clean-checkout step (checkout-status.json) repeats it as a second check. A dirty or unrecorded run makes its arm ineligible. ID MAPPING: result.json id_mapping.ok must be true. The base and trial inventories may differ only by the B1 rewrite: the single prefix tests.test_native_maintenance. on exactly the 29 base ids of the six B1 classes (compare.py B1_CLASSES and B1_IDS, from ids.py on the trial base e88d59e4, as on the first base 56473e4b), as a bijection, with every other id the same in both. A partial rewrite, another prefix, identical inventories or any other difference sets it false, and compare.py then gives every OS the outcome no verdict. RE-RUNS: the trial is repeated only as a whole, by a new synchronize of the draft pull request, never by re-running jobs. A job re-run voids the affected arm-run, which is reported as a failed attempt: every artifact upload sets overwrite: false, so a re-run cannot replace an earlier attempt's artifact, and (j) voids any re-run artifact that reaches compare.py. Every attempt is reported. CONTROLS run in separate jobs for every arm, S included. The control file alone in an empty directory must report exactly control_expectations.json's standalone run: Ran 8; FAILED (failures=2, errors=2, skipped=1, expected failures=1, unexpected successes=1); a non-zero exit; the listed pass, skip, failure, error, failing-subtest, expected-failure, unexpected-success, multi-line-docstring and setUpClass-error records; and, in parallel, a header of 1 module suite or 3 class suites over 9 tests. The crash control (os._exit(3)) under a 300 s bound must start, exit non-zero and print no OK summary; a hang ended by the bound is fail-closed and passes. A control or crash run must also meet (a), (b), (c), (j) and part 2, or it fails. DECISION RULE, per OS. An arm is eligible only when it has at least three runs, every run is eligible under both oracle parts (zero mismatches), and its controls and crash control passed. S must be eligible, or the OS gets no verdict. Take the fastest eligible parallel arm by median step seconds (a tie goes to the arm name that sorts first). Adopt it only if its median is at most 0.60 times the S median and its maximum is at most 0.75 times S's fastest run, compared as exact ratios of the recorded seconds with no rounding before the comparison (result.json rounds them for display only); otherwise reject, with no fall-through to a slower arm. If the adopted arm is P3 (L4 on Linux), take P3F (L4F) instead when it is eligible, meets the rule and its median is at most 1.10 times the pooled median, also compared exactly. This is the plan's 'prefer P3F if within 10% of P3', which the coordinator confirmed on 2026-10-03, before any hosted run, for P3F over P3 and for L4F over L4. If id_mapping.ok is false, neither OS gets a verdict. result.json lists every OS of the preregistration, and an OS for which no run directory arrived (timed, control or crash) gets no verdict with the reason 'no run directory'. A reject or a no-verdict outcome is kept as a failed attempt. The macOS verdict decides PR-A and the Linux verdict PR-A2, independently. METRICS: the selection metric is the test step's seconds, meta.json step_seconds (the in-step wall clock around the command) as compare.py reads it. For every run the observed record also keeps the Actions jobs API (GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs/{run_id}/jobs) started_at and completed_at for the test step and for the whole job (job seconds). These are reported beside the rule's input and are not used by the rule.

Control observations. An observed run can be passed only with exit code 0 (scripts/validate_convergence.py:120), so a control observation's exit_code is the control step's own exit (0; the step and the job concluded success), its status passed means that compare.py's control check passed for both of its run directories, and the commands' own exits (1 and 3 under S; 5 and 124 under unittest-parallel) are in its scope text and in control-logs.txt.
